newsitem.title: USA: Shoving match in House pushes out "new civility".
newsitem.headline: Shoving match in House pushes out "new civility".

text.p: A political spat over campaign finance reform ended in a shoving match in the House chamber Wednesday, in a sign that efforts to bring a new civility to the House are giving way to frayed tempers and sharp partisanship.
The encounter between Republican Whip Tom DeLay of Texas and senior Democrat David Obey of Wisconsin climaxed an argument over Democrats' efforts to set a date to consider campaign finance reform.
Obey marched over to the Republican side of the chamber and, witnesses said, harangued Delay, thrusting a two-year-old newspaper article in his face.
They said DeLay responded by giving Obey a two-handed shove to get him away. The clash ended with aides separating the pair and DeLay being pulled away.
The clash occurred just one month after members of both parties flocked to a "get-to-know-you" retreat in Hershey, Pennyslvania, aimed at making the House a more friendly place.
